step.text: A spreadsheet from Shopify or your ERP is usually all we need: every restaurant's regular items, its prices and the codes you use.

step.text: Each guide goes in, the account opens, and the chef installs the app.

@graph.name: Do we need a Shopify B2B alternative before chefs can order with their voice?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The store, its catalogs, the checkout and your terms stay put. What changes is how your phone-in customers buy: their chef opens our app, speaks each item, checks what it lists and sends it, rather than reading the order out to someone on your team.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Shopify B2B?

acceptedAnswer.text: At one job: turning a chef's spoken list into an order, for chefs who prefer speaking to browsing. The store, catalogs, checkout and payments are Shopify's work, so we stay next to it and are not a Shopify B2B alternative.

@graph.name: Is it linked to Shopify, and will my desk still type orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: No link is built in: they come from two companies, and neither supports the other's software. If we email the order, someone on your side still enters it in Shopify. What they skip is the call: no one listens, writes the items out and reads them back, since every item was gone over in the app first. Shopify has an API for creating orders, but nothing connects ours to it out of the box. If your setup can accept our orders by EDI or the API, no one types them again; a demo answers whether it can.

@graph.name: Will app orders show up in our Shopify reports?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only once they are in Shopify. Until then, our orders stay out of Shopify's order history, reports and automations, and the chef will not find them in their Shopify account. Once an order is in Shopify, Shopify gives it a number of its own. Shopify, or the ERP behind it, stays the record for your customers, your stock and your invoices. On our side we hold the guides, prices included, along with whatever the chefs send through the app.

@graph.name: Couldn't restaurants just use Shopify's quick order list?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chefs who like it should hold on to it, along with reorders from earlier purchases. Other apps answer calls with AI or read emailed POs into drafts for your team to approve. Those take the call or the file as it arrives; ours gives the chef the list on their own phone to fix before it goes.

@graph.name: Which Shopify plan do we need for this?

acceptedAnswer.text: Any of them: setting up changes nothing in your store. Your plan matters on Shopify's side for features like per-company catalogs, which Shopify lists on Plus; each account in our app gets its own guide whichever plan you are on. If you later want orders sent into Shopify over the API, the demo covers what that would take.

@graph.name: How quick is setup, and what will it cost us?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most distributors are up and running in 24 to 48 hours, and your store does not change. Send us the items each restaurant usually buys, often as an exported spreadsheet. We load them, set up every account, and the chefs install our app; most restaurants have a first order in that same day. Shopify lists what its plans cost. We publish no prices; each distributor gets its own quote. Swapping in a Shopify B2B replacement means rebuilding your store, catalogs and checkout elsewhere; the app leaves all three in place.

@graph.name: Where do the Shopify B2B details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: We read shopify.com and Shopify's B2B help pages on 9 November 2026: the wholesale page, plan pricing, and the guides to B2B plan features, store types, customer accounts, draft orders and sales staff. The third-party tools turned up in a search of the Shopify App Store and the wider web. Spot something out of date? Write to us and we will fix it.
